rationale: The "motive" leg is mislabeled — RANK(NEG(ni/sale)) peaks for large *losses*, not thin-but-positive margins (the archive's better-performing versions enforced profitability via the MIN with the profit-streak indicator) — and the capacity leg shares the sales deflator with the base, so the interaction partly re-weights the accrual by its own scale rather than conditioning on independent economics.

This is a mechanical 2x2 grid fill that pairs the archive's existing stock-overhang base with the verbatim conditioner from NetIndebtedThinMarginAccrual, with the same loss-firm contamination in RANK(NEG(ni/sale)) and high correlation between the net-debt and thin-margin legs, so it is a cosmetic recombination rather than a new mechanism.

Combining the flow (current recognition aggressiveness) and own-history stock (accumulated unconverted claims) into one base before conditioning is a genuinely distinct construction rather than a deflator tweak, and the internal logic and sign are coherent, though it remains an incremental extension of a heavily mined family and SUMRANK may blur the two very different information horizons.

Swapping the conditioner's deflator from sale to cogs is close to cosmetic since the two are near-proportional for most firms, so it cannot cleanly diagnose the shared-scaling concern it is designed to address and is otherwise a strict subset of DiscretionCapacityAccrual.

Testing whether the mechanism lives in the within-firm rather than cross-sectional normalization of the accrual flow is a legitimate and unexplored axis with a coherent sign, but it is still grid-completion on an extensively mined base-times-conditioner space and the payoff is diagnostic rather than a new economic channel.

The claim of avoiding mechanical overlap is wrong in substance — multiplying an asset-side build by a *falling* operating-liability change is a multiplicative surrogate for the full working-capital accrual already tested throughout the archive — and a decline in payables is at least as consistent with a firm paying suppliers from strength or shrinking activity as with supplier monitoring, so the "external assessor" interpretation is not identified.
